pitfalls.problem: build_gantt.py opened with a single-quoted multi-line string, so importing it from build_matrices.py raised SyntaxError and the Build matrices step exited 1 (run 42553625095).
pitfalls.failed_approach: Trusting the write_file ok=true receipt as proof the Python source parses.
pitfalls.lesson: A new module imported by build_matrices must start with a real docstring or comment; its first proof is the build step conclusion on the next push run, not the write receipt.
pitfalls.resolution: Docstring edit at 96ef7894 produced green run 42554257008.

pitfalls.problem: Commit regenerated matrices exited 1 at 42553597443, initially attributed to an unguarded commit on a clean tree.
pitfalls.failed_approach: Diagnosing from the step name instead of reading the step body; the workflow already wraps commit/push in an if git diff --cached --quiet guard.
pitfalls.lesson: Read the workflow step body before proposing a repair; with the guard present, a step-7 exit 1 means the else-branch ran and commit or push itself failed.
pitfalls.correction: Misdiagnosis corrected; no workflow change required.

pitfalls.problem: Unauthenticated job pages return 'This step has been truncated due to its large size' for every step, so the failing log line is never visible.
pitfalls.failed_approach: Trying to read the cause from the job HTML page.
pitfalls.lesson: Use run_jobs step conclusions plus the annotation list; never quote a log line that was not actually returned.

pitfalls.problem: The workflow's own commit step pushes a commit, so the branch head no longer matches the sha the proven check-run covers (it pushed 187168f5, then 60b4d6cc, while the green check-run head stayed e3eba97e).
pitfalls.failed_approach: Treating a green run on the branch as sufficient for the merge gate.
pitfalls.lesson: Before merge_pr, take branch_head and the branch run list in the same turn and match run.sha to the exact head. A green run whose sha is an ancestor does not authorize the merge.

pitfalls.problem: Head 60b4d6cc, created by the workflow's own commit step, has no workflow run, so the exact-head check can never be met by polling.
pitfalls.failed_approach: Polling branch_head plus runs repeatedly for a run whose sha equals the self-commit head.
pitfalls.lesson: A push by a workflow step with the default GITHUB_TOKEN does not trigger a run. Push one allowed-path change yourself; once generated outputs are already committed the guarded commit makes no diff and the head stays put.

pitfalls.problem: PROGRESS.json under docs/venice-audit-v1/ is rewritten by the build step, so authored text there does not survive and editing it re-fires the guarded commit.
pitfalls.failed_approach: Forcing a fresh push run by editing docs/venice-audit-v1/PROGRESS.json.
pitfalls.lesson: Distinguish authored files from build outputs before choosing a push target. Force runs from tests/test_repo_requirements_audit.py or the workflow file.
